title: A famous schoolroom myth. Einstein did not fail mathematics.
description:
Einstein did not fail mathematics. Ripley's Believe It or Not printed the claim anyway.

Showed Einstein the Ripley's clipping. He laughed and said he never failed in mathematics.

Einstein said he had mastered differential and integral calculus before reaching this age.

At 16 he missed the standard in the general part of the 1895 ETH entrance test. He performed with distinction in physics and mathematics.

In 1896 he earned the top grade, a 6, in algebra and geometry.

Sources:
- https://content.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,1936731_1936743_1936758,00.html (read): established that Ripley's Believe It or Not repeated the claim that Einstein failed mathematics, that in 1935 a Princeton rabbi showed him the clipping and he laughed and replied "I never failed in mathematics", and that he said "Before I was fifteen I had mastered differential and integral calculus".
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Einstein (read): established that at 16 he failed to reach the required standard in the general part of the 1895 ETH entrance test but performed with distinction in physics and mathematics, that he mastered integral and differential calculus by his own account in his early teens, and that he received the top grade of 6 in algebra and geometry in his 1896 Matura.
